knowledge_point.title: Finding a Scalar Factor in a Linear Combination

question.:question/problem:
The arrows show $\overrightarrow{OA}=\mathbf a$, $\overrightarrow{OB}=\mathbf b$, and $\overrightarrow{OC}=\mathbf c$. Grid squares have side length one unit.

![](images/87/870ab808de9f829e5967f4792119b4b596ad9de28ff714e1ce5c3b2b686338fb.png)

Given that $\mathbf{c}=\lambda\mathbf{a}+\frac{4}{3}\mathbf{b}$, find $\lambda$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Construct the known component $\frac{4}{3}\mathbf{b}$ from $O$, and call its endpoint $P$. Count signed horizontal and vertical grid displacements:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\overrightarrow{OP} &=\frac{4}{3}\,(3, 0)=(4, 0). \\
\overrightarrow{PC} &=(4, -8).
\end{aligned}
$$

![](images/80/808f2835fcaf678e3cbde7898ac8af3893e9dc71ed879cff900aefc430393c74.png)

Compare the remaining displacement with $\mathbf{a}$, whose grid displacement is $(2, -4)$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Horizontal scale} &=\frac{4}{2}=2 \\
\text{Vertical scale} &=\frac{-8}{-4}=2
\end{aligned}
$$

The scale is positive, so the remaining vector has the same direction as $\mathbf{a}$. Thus $\overrightarrow{PC}=2\mathbf{a}$. By the triangle law,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathbf{c} &=\overrightarrow{OP}+\overrightarrow{PC} \\
&=\frac{4}{3}\mathbf{b}+2\mathbf{a} \\
&=2\mathbf{a}+\frac{4}{3}\mathbf{b}.
\end{aligned}
$$

The vectors $\mathbf{a}$ and $\mathbf{b}$ are not parallel, so their coefficients are unique. Matching the coefficient of $\mathbf{a}$ gives $\lambda=2$.

conversions: Reduce grid displacement ratio to a positive rational scalar
solution_path.support: e-5212; lesson path tracing; prerequisite scalar multiplication

question.:question/worked-solution:
Construct the known component $\mathbf{b}$ from $O$, ending at $B$. Count signed horizontal and vertical grid displacements:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\overrightarrow{OB} &=1\,(3, 0)=(3, 0). \\
\overrightarrow{BC} &=(12, -12).
\end{aligned}

$$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Horizontal scale} &=\frac{12}{4}=3 \\
\text{Vertical scale} &=\frac{-12}{-4}=3
\end{aligned}
$$

The scale is positive, so the remaining vector has the same direction as $\mathbf{a}$. Thus $\overrightarrow{BC}=3\mathbf{a}$. By the triangle law,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathbf{c} &=\overrightarrow{OB}+\overrightarrow{BC} \\
&=\mathbf{b}+3\mathbf{a} \\
&=3\mathbf{a}+\mathbf{b}.
\end{aligned}
$$

The vectors $\mathbf{a}$ and $\mathbf{b}$ are not parallel, so their coefficients are unique. Matching the coefficient of $\mathbf{a}$ gives $\lambda=3$.
